user_questions.question: Who are the 'agents' and what kind of component do you want? (A) Human agents in the console: a Lightning record-page component on Storefront__c (reusing and fixing the existing, unplaced menuBrowser LWC). (B) The Agentforce Merchant Support Agent: an action plus lightning__AgentforceOutput renderer that shows the menu by category in chat (the org already has giftCardRenderer/orderStatusRenderer of this kind). Recommendation: A, because the requirement says 'component' and menuBrowser already exists.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Menu browser in the service console grouped by category.

skill_friction: AskCoworker D1 and D2 both claimed no menu-browsing LWC exists (D2 only checked AuraDefinitionBundle); the skill's 'Missed components' guidance caught it, but the org-verification reference has no explicit hint to query LightningComponentBundle for UI requirements.
AskCoworker answers repeatedly tagged facts as '[Verified: prior session]' even for facts supplied in the same message; the response-handling table covers echoed facts but this label is noisy.

spec-format says a grant to a 'broad permission set' is an open decision and a new dedicated PS is an acceptable default, while SKILL.md Rule 4 says 'Reuse existing components'; it is unclear which wins when AskCoworker proposes adding to an existing app PS. I chose a new dedicated PS.

The skill's fork rule: 'agents' (human vs Agentforce) was a genuine fork in an Agentforce-heavy org; the criteria fit, but SKILL.md gives no guidance on whether ambiguous personas count as 'two interpretations need different objects' (here they need different component types, not objects).
FlexiPage activation/assignment (org default vs app default) cannot be read with allowed commands; no guidance on how to treat record-page activation in the inventory, so it became an assumption.
